scope: Codex desktop in-app Browser accessibility interaction path

findings.title: volatile numeric element indexes
non-actionable stale-operation errors
no universal stable locator in accessibility output
high-frequency diffs can be partially consistent
no capture time or generation metadata
no semantic conditional wait primitive
full accessibility observation latency
large full-tree context footprint
no accessibility subtree filters or pagination
collapsed selects expand all options into context
covered elements can be clicked through visual overlays
pointer-only custom controls have ambiguous semantics
contenteditable lacks direct editable semantics
accessibility relationships lost in text projection
closed shadow content omitted without opaque marker
form values exposed without policy-aware redaction
full link query exposed without policy-aware redaction
resource diagnostics omit response and performance data
no console or network log capability
built-in browser and signed-in Chrome contexts are separate

notes: These findings describe the tested Codex desktop in-app Browser path, not every OpenAI computer-use integration.
Some limitations can be bypassed with Playwright locators or screenshots; the fallback cost remains part of the finding.
Latency figures are local observations and BrowserKit returns a smaller custom projection, so they are not an equal-information benchmark.
C16 and C17 are privacy-policy gaps rather than evidence of a current sensitive-data incident.
